ai.title: Remove responseformat from relace-api toolFormatter
ai.summary: The `response_format` parameter, previously set to `json_schema` with `outputSchema`, was removed from the `toolFormatter` function in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts`. This change simplifies the API call payload by omitting the explicit JSON schema enforcement. The update is internal to the backend's LLM API integration for Relace.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use a specific tool, it used to send along a strict set of formatting rules so the response came back perfectly structured. That rule was removed, so now it simply asks for the tool result without forcing a particular layout. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were watching the raw data the assistant sends behind the scenes. The change is internal and already live today.

ai.title: Restore responseformat in relace-api toolFormatter
ai.summary: Re-added `response_format` parameter to `toolFormatter` in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts`. Ensures structured JSON output enforcement for relace API calls.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to produce a specific kind of reply, it now reliably follows that structure again. A setting that tells the assistant how to format its answer was reconnected in one spot after being accidentally removed, so structured answers come back through correctly.

ai.title: Tweak FT data collection script
ai.summary: Moved BLOBBIFY_MESSAGE_HISTORY logic in scripts/ft-file-selection/collect-tuning-data.ts to run before message combining. Increased trace fetch limit from 100 to 3000 in main().

eli5.text: The data collection script now processes conversation history in a smarter order, cleaning up how assistant messages are stored before combining them together. It also pulls in up to 3,000 conversation traces at once instead of 100, letting it gather much larger datasets in one pass. These are behind-the-scenes adjustments for whoever tunes the AI model's training data.

ai.title: Parse error flag set in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: The `foundParsingError` flag is now set to `true` inside the error callback in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This ensures parsing errors encountered during tool execution are correctly tracked. The change is internal to the backend prompt logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs background tools, it now keeps a clearer record when one of those tools fails to read a response correctly. Previously that kind of hiccup could slip by unnoticed, but now the system marks it as a parsing problem so it can be tracked and fixed. This only affects how the internal logging works, so you won't see a visible change in your chat, but the assistant's error reporting behind the scenes is a bit more accurate.

ai.title: Fix Relace API response format serialization
ai.summary: Relace API tool formatter now serializes `outputSchema` to a JSON string before passing it to `response_format`. Max tokens reduced from 32k to 8192. Added `messageId` to error logging context in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts`.

eli5.text: The helper that converts the assistant's tool usage into the right format for the Relace API now properly packages its response schema as a JSON string before sending it, fixing a formatting mismatch that was causing errors. This change also lowers the maximum tokens the tool-formatter can use from 32,000 to 8,192, which may reduce the size of generated responses in edge cases. Additionally, error logs from this helper now include the message ID, making it easier to trace and debug specific failures.

ai.title: Add maxAgentSteps to CodebuffConfigSchema
ai.summary: Added maxAgentSteps to CodebuffConfigSchema, allowing users to configure the maximum number of turns the agent takes before ending. This change updates the JSON config snapshot to reflect the new optional parameter.

eli5.text: You (the people running the assistant tool) can now tell the assistant how many rounds of back-and-forth it is allowed to have before it has to stop. A new optional setting lets you cap the total number of turns in a session, and if you leave it blank the assistant will still stop after 12 turns by default. This limit is in place now and ready to use.

ai.title: Fix Relace API tool formatter response handling
ai.summary: Updated `toolFormatter` in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts` to correctly parse Relace API responses. Changed `response_format` to use structured `json_schema` with `name` and `schema` keys instead of stringified JSON. Adjusted response parsing to extract `tool_calls` from `JSON.parse` of message content.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks the Relace coding tool to suggest edits, it now formats the request and reads the response correctly instead of getting garbled output. The assistant previously sent the response shape as a plain text string and tried to read tool suggestions directly from the reply body, which broke the connection. It now packages the shape properly and pulls the suggestions out by first decoding the reply body as text. If you watched closely, conversations with this tool would no longer drop or misread the suggested edits mid-flow.

ai.title: Saxy adds shouldParseEntities flag
ai.summary: Saxy constructor accepts optional shouldParseEntities boolean, defaulting to true. When false, parser skips parseEntities calls and incomplete entity detection. Affects text buffer emission in common/src/util/saxy.ts. Refactor of internal XML entity handling.

eli5.text: You can now turn off how the assistant reads special characters in XML-style text. When this option is disabled, the assistant treats ampersands and semicolons as ordinary characters instead of converting them, which is useful when processing code or data that shouldn't be interpreted as text formatting. This gives you finer control over how text content is handled without needing to disable all entity handling.

ai.title: Add prompting to Relace tool formatter
ai.summary: Relace API tool formatter prompt updated with instructions for multi-line parameters and explicit parameter handling. Adds guidance for write_file multi-line params and clarifies that no parameters are required. Changes confined to backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts.

eli5.text: The instructions that guide how the assistant picks and fills in tools when responding to you have been updated to handle multi-line inputs better, especially when creating or editing files with multiple lines of text. The system now reminds itself not to skip these multi-line parameters and also clarifies that no parameters are required unless explicitly listed. This improves the accuracy of tool usage, particularly for tasks involving file creation or editing that contain multiple lines of content. The change is live today and applies to interactions involving internal tool formatting.

ai.title: Command permission prompt shows raw command, not tool call
ai.summary: System prompt in backend/src/tools.ts now instructs agent to display commands for permission via triple-backtick blocks, explicitly forbidding tool call format. Example added showing `git branch -D foo`. Scope limited to that prompt string.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs permission to run a command, it now shows that command in a plain code block instead of using the tool-call format. If you see a permission prompt, you'll notice the command displayed as clean code rather than wrapped in tool-call syntax. This affects anyone who gets asked to approve commands while the assistant is working.

ai.title: Update tools test snapshots for shell permission prompt
ai.summary: Updated `tools.test.ts.snap` to reflect changes in the shell tool's permission request instructions. The snapshot now includes explicit guidance to avoid the tool call format for permission requests, using a `git branch -D foo` example. This change is internal, affecting only test fixtures.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks you for permission before running a risky command, it now shows you exactly how to do it: paste the command in a code box and skip the special tool format. A deleted-branch example (git branch -D foo) demonstrates the new wording. This only affects internal test files, so nothing feels different to you today.

ai.title: Ask mode restricts writefile, strreplace, createplan
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts enforces tool restrictions in ask mode. write_file, str_replace, create_plan, and run_terminal_command calls return error results instead of executing. Exception applies when prompt matches /export or export, allowing summary generation. Internal backend change affects all surfaces using ask mode.

ai.title: File change hooks run commands on modified files
ai.summary: Added `fileChangeHooks` to `codebuff.json` schema in `common/src/json-config/constants.ts`. New `npm-app/src/json-config/hooks.ts` executes configured commands synchronously after file writes, filtering by `filePattern` via `micromatch`. Failed hooks append `ToolResult` entries to agent state, forcing further agent steps. `npm-app/src/client.ts` tracks changed file paths and triggers hook execution.

eli5.text: When you (or the assistant) edit a file, the editor can now automatically run extra instructions right after each save. For example, it can run a spell-check or code-style check on just the file you changed, without you typing that command yourself. Project owners turn this on by listing those instructions in the project's settings file, where each instruction runs only when certain kinds of files are edited. All of this is live today: if a hook fails, its error gets reported back so you see it right away.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.308
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.307 to 1.0.308. Change isolated to npm-app/package.json. No functional code or dependency modifications.

eli5.text: The software was given a new internal version label (from 1.0.307 to 1.0.308). This is a behind-the-scenes update that doesn't change how the software works or what it can do, it's like renumbering a receipt without altering the purchase. No users will notice anything different after this update. It's a routine housekeeping change that helps the development team keep their records straight. If you looked at the project files, you'd only see the version number has changed, nothing else. This kind of change happens frequently in software development to track releases, even when no actual features or fixes are included.

ai.title: Swap typecheck hooks for unit tests in backend npm-app common
ai.summary: Replaced typecheck commands with `bun test` execution for `backend`, `npm-app`, and added `common` in `codebuff.json`. Hooks now target `src/*.test.ts` files, explicitly excluding `*.integration.test.ts`. This ensures unit test coverage triggers on file changes across these subsystems instead of static analysis.

eli5.text: When developers modify TypeScript files in the backend, npm-app, or common directories, the project now runs unit tests immediately instead of just checking types. The test runner looks at your code, finds the small test files (but ignores integration test files), and runs them on the spot to confirm your changes didn't break anything. Developers will now notice whether their edits pass or fail these faster checks right away, getting more direct feedback before they move on.

ai.title: Fix fileChangeHook bugs
ai.summary: Updated `runFileChangeHooks` in `npm-app/src/json-config/hooks.ts` to return an object `{ toolResults, someHooksFailed }` instead of just an array. Hook execution logic now unconditionally pushes results to `toolResults` while setting `someHooksFailed` if `result.exitCode !== 0`. `npm-app/src/client.ts` consumes this change to correctly determine `isComplete` status based on hook failures rather than result presence. `fileChangeHooks` in `common/src/json-config/constants.ts` marked `.optional()`.

eli5.text: If you've set up commands to run automatically when your files change (like a formatting tool or a linter that runs on save), there was a bug where the assistant wouldn't correctly tell that one of those commands had failed. Now the assistant properly checks whether each command succeeded or errored out, instead of just checking if any command ran at all. The net effect: when a background command trips on your files, the assistant will correctly pause and let you know something went wrong, rather than pretending everything finished cleanly. This is live today for anyone using file-change hooks in their configuration.

ai.title: Version 1.0.309
ai.summary: Bumped package version to 1.0.309 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: If you update the assistant today, the first thing you'll notice is that it now checks its own work by running small test scripts when you ask it to make changes, instead of just checking that the code looks consistent. Behind the scenes, the developers also fixed a glitch where the assistant could get confused when tracking which files you asked it to edit, so those requests now complete more reliably.

ai.title: Strip ANSI colors from terminal command output
ai.summary: ANSI escape sequences are stripped from stdout in formatResult via stripColors before truncation. Prevents agent confusion from raw control characters. Affects npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts. Truncation limit COMMAND_OUTPUT_LIMIT applies to clean text.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads the result of a command it runs on a computer, it now sees clean text without any leftover color codes or formatting marks that terminals sometimes embed. Previously those raw control characters could appear in the text and confuse the assistant, so it now cleans the output before looking at it. This affects the internal tooling used by the assistant behind the scenes and is live today.

ai.title: Set project root in checkpoint worker
ai.summary: Added `setProjectRoot` call in `checkpoint-worker.ts` before checkpoint operations. Ensures file state functions resolve paths correctly within the worker context.

eli5.text: The worker that saves and restores your project's code state now sets its project directory at the right place before doing its work. This affects internal checkpoint operations and ensures file paths resolve correctly. You would not notice this externally, as it is behind-the-scenes housekeeping.
